title: Create platform signing and installed-path acceptance suite
notes: MBR-901 (macOS, repair commit 4bbf84c1 over 2d543114) and MBR-902 (Windows, repair over dd0bf495) already deliver two things each, per docs/release/macos.md and docs/release/windows.md: (a) a read-back/re-verification of RightKit's real sealed build output, never re-signing anything, and (b) the membrane-specific evidence RightKit does not produce -- scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs's shared orthic.membrane.platform-acceptance.v1 receipt schema (trust + install/startup/update/uninstall lifecycle), and, on Windows only, scripts/release/windows/contract.mjs's validateLifecycleReceipt proving every inner PE individually signtool-verified. This task (MBR-806) does not re-implement or fork any of that. It adds the one layer that did not exist: a fail-closed binding gate that requires both the shared receipt AND the platform-specific deeper evidence together, cross-checked by commit/artifact identity, before accepting anything as installed-path acceptance.

WHY A BINDING LAYER WAS MISSING AND NEEDED: verify-platform-artifacts.mjs's Windows trust schema is exactly { authenticode, publicTrust, rfc3161} -- three flags about the OUTER installer only (see packaging/contracts/platform-acceptance.v1.json). validateLifecycleReceipt's per-inner-PE proof lives in a SEPARATE schema (windows-installer-receipt.v1) that verify-platform-artifacts.mjs never touches. Consumed independently -- e.g. by `node scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs --all` alone, the book gate's own manifest command for this task -- a Windows release could present a fully schema-valid platform-acceptance receipt (trust.authenticode: 'pass', attesting only the outer NSIS installer) while every inner PE the installer actually runs (membrane-hub.exe, crypt-service.exe, membrane.exe) remains unsigned, per the confirmed RightKit NSIS-timing defect docs/release/windows.md records. scripts/release/acceptance/windows-installed-acceptance.mjs closes exactly this: it requires and cross-binds both documents, and throws if the lifecycle receipt is missing, names fewer PEs than Tauri's bundle.externalBin + 1 requires, or has any payload whose signtool verify is not 'pass' -- even when the outer platform-acceptance receipt alone would be schema-valid. This is proven directly by the test 'FAILS CLOSED when the outer installer is signed but one inner-PE payload was never verified (the confirmed RightKit NSIS gap)' in tests/platform/acceptance/windows-installed-acceptance.test.mjs, which constructs exactly that scenario -- a fully valid outer platformReceipt paired with a lifecycle receipt where one sidecar's verify is 'fail' -- and asserts the combined gate rejects it.

macOS has no equivalent outer/inner split (RightKit/Tauri codesign every externalBin sidecar and the outer .app inner-to-outer, with hardened runtime, before notarization -- docs/release/macos.md), so scripts/release/acceptance/macos-installed-acceptance.mjs instead closes the remaining ways a 'signed' claim could be hollow: the shared receipt's trust/lifecycle fields, a cross-check that the receipt's artifact is byte-for-byte what RightKit sealed for this exact commit/version (readSealedReleaseManifest / verifySealedInstallerHash, imported from scripts/release/macos/contract.mjs, never re-signed here), and a re-verification of the macOS release receipt against the actual .app/.dmg bytes by spawning scripts/release/macos/release-macos.mjs's existing `verify-receipt` command as a subprocess (reused rather than reimplemented, since its directory-hash walk is internal to that script; verify-receipt never touches codesign/spctl/hdiutil/xcrun, only hash comparison).

MINIMIZE rung: REUSE. Both new scripts compose existing, already-tested, already-landed exports (verify-platform-artifacts.mjs's validateReceipt, macos/contract.mjs's validatePlatformAcceptanceReceipt/readSealedReleaseManifest/verifySealedInstallerHash, windows/contract.mjs's validateSealedManifest/validateExpectedPayloads/validateLifecycleReceipt/minimumExpectedPayloadCount/readJson, and macos/release-macos.mjs's verify-receipt CLI subcommand via subprocess) -- nothing in scripts/release/macos/**, scripts/release/windows/**, or scripts/release/verify-platform-artifacts.mjs was modified or forked. The only new logic is the minimum unavoidable glue: cross-document identity binding (commit/artifact-name/artifact-sha256/version consistency across the shared receipt and the platform-specific deeper evidence) that did not exist in any prior module. No new dependency was added; both scripts use only node:fs, node:fs/promises, node:child_process, node:path, and node:url from the standard library.

Test suite: tests/platform/acceptance/windows-installed-acceptance.test.mjs (14 tests) and tests/platform/acceptance/macos-installed-acceptance.test.mjs (9 tests), 23/23 passing -- see commands.log. Windows coverage: full pass; the confirmed inner-PE gap as both 'one payload unverified' and 'payload entirely absent'; too few proven payloads versus Tauri's sidecar count; a missing lifecycle receipt (fails closed, never assumes pass); source-ready masquerading as installed; bypass warnings; incomplete Windows trust; and identity mismatch (artifact sha256, commit) between the outer receipt and RightKit's sealed manifest -- at both the pure-function level and via real-subprocess CLI invocation of this task's own script against real temp files. macOS coverage: full pass; a tampered sealed DMG; an identity-mismatched artifact; a macOS receipt whose recorded hash does not match the actual .app/.dmg bytes; a macOS receipt with an incomplete check (Gatekeeper skipped); a missing macOS receipt file; incomplete macOS trust; source-ready masquerading as installed; and a decoy DMG with matching bytes but the wrong sealed path.

docs/release/acceptance.md documents the binding layer, the confirmed gap it closes, both CLI commands, and the real credentialled commands (pnpm release:build:mac / pnpm release:build:win and this task's two CLIs) that remain deferred to the Book 3 final phased gate.

Not touched, out of allowed scope per this task's dispatch instructions: scripts/release/macos/**, scripts/release/windows/**, scripts/release/channels/**, scripts/release/homebrew/**, scripts/release/updater/**, top-level scripts/release/*.mjs, packaging/**, apps/membrane-hub/**, data/book-progress.json (orchestrator-owned ledger), and evidence/platform/windows/windows-release-manifest.json (a stale fixture in a superseded schema, already flagged for reconciliation by MBR-902's own evidence and docs/release/windows.md's 'Compatibility note' -- left as-is since fixing it is unrelated to this task's acceptance-suite deliverable and no code or test in this repository references it, confirmed via grep).

No cargo build/test, no pnpm/Tauri build, no right-release, no codesign/notarytool/spctl/hdiutil/xcrun/stapler/signtool/AzureSignTool invocation, and no mutating git command was run at any point in this task. The two node --test runs in commands.log are the only commands executed.
